title: CP Algorithms
description: Comprehensive reference for competitive programming algorithms and data structures, with detailed explanations and C++ implementations.

title: CSES Problem Set
description: ~300 curated competitive programming problems covering all major topics — widely considered the best structured problem set for learning.

title: Codeforces
description: The leading competitive programming platform. Regular Div. 1–4 contests, editorial write-ups, and a massive problem archive.

title: Competitive Programmer's Handbook
description: Free PDF textbook by Antti Laaksonen covering graph theory, dynamic programming, number theory, and more for competitive programmers.

title: picoCTF
description: Beginner-friendly CTF platform by Carnegie Mellon University. Challenges in web, crypto, forensics, reverse engineering, and binary exploitation.

title: pwn.college
description: Structured learning platform for binary exploitation and systems security — covering GDB, shellcode, ROP chains, kernel exploitation.

title: CryptoPals Challenges
description: Hands-on cryptography challenges that teach you to break real cryptographic systems through practical implementation. Highly recommended.

title: CTFtime.org
description: Calendar and archive of CTF competitions worldwide. Find upcoming events, team rankings, and write-ups from past competitions.

title: fast.ai Practical Deep Learning
description: Top-down approach to deep learning: practical course that gets you building state-of-the-art models from lesson one, no PhD required.

title: Andrej Karpathy: Zero to Hero
description: Build neural networks from scratch in Python, culminating in a GPT-style language model. The clearest explanation of backprop that exists.

title: CS:APP — Bryant & O'Hallaron
description: Computer Systems: A Programmer's Perspective — the definitive systems programming textbook. Assembly, memory, caching, linking, concurrency.

title: MIT 6.824 Distributed Systems
description: MIT's graduate distributed systems course. Lectures and labs covering Raft consensus, MapReduce, and fault-tolerant key-value storage.

title: The Missing Semester of CS
description: MIT's course on practical tools CS education skips: the shell, Vim, Git internals, debugging, profiling, and more. Essential for every student.

title: Project Euler
description: Mathematical and computational problems requiring creative algorithmic thinking. Great for sharpening both mathematical reasoning and coding skills.
